en: When Congress passes a bill, the President signs it into law, making it a legally binding rule for all Filipinos.
Tearing their tax certificates at Pugad Lawin caused Andres Bonifacio and the Katipuneros to officially begin the Philippine Revolution against Spain.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses a kerosene lamp to maintain heat, saving premature babies during power outages.
The Ifugao built stone-walled rice terraces that slow down water runoff, preventing soil erosion on the steep mountains of the Cordilleras.
When citizens cast votes, the COMELEC counts the ballots to determine which candidates will officially represent them in the government.
Offering colorful kiping decorations to their houses expresses farmers' gratitude to San Isidro Labrador, resulting in the vibrant visual celebration of Pahiyas.
Ancient Filipinos carved specific Baybayin symbols onto bamboo, which allowed them to write complete syllables instead of individual letters.
Dr. Angel Alcala established artificial coral reefs, which provide new habitats for fish to breed and help restore depleted marine ecosystems.
The Bill of Rights restricts government power, which prevents state abuse and ensures every Filipino enjoys fundamental freedoms like speech.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish abuses, which awakened Filipino nationalism and inspired the revolution.
Filipinos bring pasalubong gifts from trips to show they thought of their family, which strengthens their emotional bond upon returning home.
Guillermo Tolentino arranged multiple bronze figures pointing upward on the Bonifacio Monument, which visually symbolizes the Katipuneros' united call for freedom.
